sources.station: non-sol-p3-preview analytic clearance and Hill screening

assumptions: All additions are hypothetical gameplay representatives, not discoveries or calibrated occurrence draws.
Catalog documents, protected names and accepted Copper Vale P3/P4/P6 are immutable.

Missing luminosity uses the Stefan-Boltzmann radius/temperature estimate when available; otherwise missing positive stellar constraints use a solar analog only in a screening clone. Catalog values are never replaced.
Unknown companion separation assumes a distant companion for circumprimary screening; known companion radial envelopes restrict additions to a tenth of closest separation.
Evolved stars use current instantaneous luminosity and clearance; survival history and long-term stability are not claimed.
Known planet constraints are screened as provided; an incomplete planet constraint uses a conservative screening-only Earth analog and its available orbit.

Close binaries also attempt a distant aggregate Kepler orbit using the existing catalog anchor and supported circumbinary orbital metadata. Effective mass/luminosity are screening-only sums; the anchored trajectory is approximate, not a moving barycenter simulation.

Bulk stellar extent is luminosity-adaptive rather than the immutable pilot 100 AU limit; compact stars may use orbits inside the pilot 0.05 AU floor subject to the same five-radius and thermal screens.
Planet is a supported gameplay family, not a claim of measured dynamical clearing; the pilot clearing discriminant is not a bulk occurrence/taxonomy blocker.

Catalog planet-family companions above one percent of primary mass are treated as companions in screening, never reclassified in the catalog. This is a conservative authored screening threshold, not an occurrence calibration.
Cold outer worlds remain supported: the bulk thermal screen has no artificial 10 K floor; ambient background heating is assumed and no liquid-water or habitable climate claim is made.

If the standard domain is exhausted, a bounded extended outer game-world reservoir up to fifty times the largest catalog planetary apoapsis is attempted with the same clearance, separation and temperature screens. Galactic tides, encounters and long-term population survival are uncertain, not runtime representation blockers.
Temperature, Roche, Hill, radial separation and mass-budget screens are analytic approximations, not N-body certification.
Software budgets ensure planet/moon/minor-body attempts, not actual population estimates.
One initial station only; no density expansion, station-keeping simulation or runtime unlock mechanics.

Naming uses cumulative rounded 60/40 inherited/narrative quotas across eligible generated larger bodies, accepted Hamilton language weights in 100-slot narrative blocks and for unprofiled system inheritance, existing provisional language-bank sketches and unique systematic qualifiers.
